land.text: the Hamgyong coast: 'East okjeo became part of the eastern part of the Lelang Commandery' (Okjeo page, no year)

predecessors.note: Okjeo 'was controlled by Gojoseon' from the 3rd century BCE to 108 BCE and 'At 107 BCE, it became part of the Xuantu Commandery'. The page does not say when it left Han control; -36 is Cliopatria's first year.

land.text: Okjeo under Gojoseon, 3rd century BCE to 108 BCE (Okjeo page)

predecessors.note: Earlier overlord, not the direct predecessor at -36.

land.text: 'In early 5th century, Okjeo was completely conquered by Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo' (Okjeo page)

successors.note: 401 is a bridging year for 'early 5th century', the same as the Dongye dossier uses. Goguryeo had made Okjeo a tributary in the 1st or 2nd century (Taejo, 56).

keyframe_review.note: The Okjeo page gives no area in km2 ('perhaps a thousand li', 'Its households number five thousand') and no map extent beyond 'roughly the area of the Hamgyŏng provinces of North Korea', so the infobox comparison is not possible. Cliopatria's 32,149 km2 (bbox 126.3-129.9E, 39.4-41.3N) sits within the page's 'Hamgyŏng provinces'; the page puts Northern Okjeo separately in 'the Duman River region' ('Buk-okjeo occupied the Duman River region'). Dong-okjeo 'bordered the other minor state of Dongye on the south'. Goguryeo attacked Northern Okjeo in 28 BCE (Goguryeo ledger), not this one.
32,029 km2, -120 km2: boundary noise against Goguryeo's 23 shape (Goguryeo +63 k km2 in the south, not here). No page dates anything on this coast for 23..42.

31,981 km2, -48 km2: boundary noise. 56: Taejo 'conquered the states of Eastern Okjeo' (Taejo page), 'reduced Okjeo to a tributary' (Okjeo page); the shape is kept because a tributary keeps its land (the Goguryeo ledger carries the vassal tint).

Same outline as 43..126, to 153. 244-245: Wei's Wang Qi pursued the Goguryeo king to South Okjeo, where 'the Okjeo tribes were all defeated, with 3,000 tribesmen killed or captured' (Goguryeo–Wei War page): no border change.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 153 shape unchanged for 154..400, as a tributary of Goguryeo (years changed only)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 154..400. Cliopatria ends Dong-okjeo in 153 and adds its 31,981 km2 to Goguryeo's shape in 154, but the Okjeo page has Okjeo a tributary of Goguryeo and conquered completely only 'in early 5th century'. The Okjeo land is kept as its own tributary state until 401 and removed from Goguryeo's direct shape (goguryeo_154 and the later adjust verdicts).

region.text: 'Dong-okjeo (Eastern Okjeo) occupied roughly the area of the Hamgyŏng provinces of North Korea'

ledger.note: -36: Dong-okjeo enters the map on the Hamgyong coast. The Okjeo page dates the people only 'perhaps the 2nd century BCE to the 5th century CE'; it was under Gojoseon to 108 BCE and then in the Xuantu and Lelang Commanderies. -36 is Cliopatria's first year; the page is silent on when it became independent.

401: Goguryeo conquers Okjeo outright. 'In early 5th century, Okjeo was completely conquered by Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo.' The page gives no year inside the century; 401 matches the Dongye dossier's bridging year. It had been a Goguryeo tributary since Taejo's reign (56, Taejo page).

wars.name: Taejo's conquest of Eastern Okjeo
wars.outcome: Taejo 'conquered the states of Eastern Okjeo in 56' (Taejo page); the Okjeo page says he 'reduced Okjeo to a tributary, which delivered local products to Goguryeo'.
wars.note: The Okjeo page dates this only to 'the 1st or 2nd century CE'.

wars.name: Goguryeo–Wei War
wars.outcome: Wang Qi pursued King Dongcheon to South Okjeo and defeated the Okjeo tribes (3,000 killed or captured); the army returned to Xuantu; no border changed, though the Ye and Okjeo tributaries came under Lelang and Daifang's influence.

wars.name: Gwanggaeto's conquest of Okjeo
wars.outcome: Okjeo 'was completely conquered by Gwanggaeto the Great of Goguryeo' in the early 5th century.
wars.note: The Gwanggaeto page does not mention Okjeo; the year is bridging.

certainty.note: A coastal chiefdom with no recorded frontier; the southern boundary with the Ye and the western one with Goguryeo are approximate throughout.

sources.title: Okjeo
sources.note: Identity, extent ('roughly the area of the Hamgyŏng provinces'), Gojoseon and Xuantu, Taejo's tribute, Gwanggaeto's conquest, 244; no infobox capital, predecessor or area.

sources.title: Goguryeo–Wei War
sources.note: 244-245: the Okjeo tribes defeated by Wei; outcome for the Okjeo and Ye tributaries.

sources.title: Goguryeo
sources.note: Taejodae's conquests of the Okjeo and Dongye tribes (undated); the 28 BCE conquest of Northern Okjeo.

notes:
Okjeo is carried as a tributary state of Goguryeo from 56 to 401 rather than as part of Goguryeo, because the Okjeo page has it 'reduced ... to a tributary' and 'completely conquered' only in the early 5th century. Cliopatria ends the row in 153 and gives the land to Goguryeo from 154. The Goguryeo dossier carries the vassal_start (56) and vassal_end (401) with counterpart dong-okjeo, and removes the Okjeo land from its own shapes 154..395; this dossier adds the keyframe dong-okjeo_154 (154..400) so the vassal tint has a shape to draw.
Start -36 is Cliopatria's year (confidence 1); the page says only 'perhaps the 2nd century BCE'. No capital is recorded on the page: capitals is empty. End 401 is a bridge for 'early 5th century' (confidence 1). No page opened dates the Han commanderies' loss of Okjeo (the Lelang page, opened for Goguryeo, does not mention Okjeo; the Dongbu Dowi and the 30 CE release are not on the pages).
Buk-okjeo (Northern Okjeo, the Duman/Tumen region) is a separate polity on the page; it has no Cliopatria row and no dossier. The Goguryeo ledger records the 28 BCE conquest under the counterpart name 'Northern Okjeo (Buk-okjeo)'.
